A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A–C. Content can be matched reliably despite local rewriting, reflow, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, FID and memorization measurements, Gaussian simulations, and numerical score-spectrum analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original generation and memorization experiments and reports revised numerical spectrum and sampling-expansiveness results in Appendix B.2.4.

M1.justification: Noise Unconditioning, Temperature Smoothing, their training losses, KNN approximations, architectures, and implemented sampling procedures are retained. The new step-size/temperature relation in A.5 is analytical guidance, not a reported algorithm modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use Cat–Caracal, CIFAR-10, CelebA, ImageNet, CelebA-HQ, and Gaussian simulations. B.2.4 still investigates CIFAR-10 overlap regions; its revised sample count and temperature sweep change the protocol rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 B.2.4 compares fixed-noise conditioning against unconditioning and temperature smoothing. v2 removes the conditioning comparator from that experiment. Conditioning remains a comparator in the unchanged generation and memorization experiments elsewhere.

E3.justification: B.2.4 substantially revises its validation protocol: CIFAR-10 centers increase from 100 to 200, while 1,000 evaluation points are retained. Four tabulated temperatures and a high-temperature check become 19 temperatures through 10^6. v2 additionally evaluates covariance-spectrum components and the one-step expansion factor at η=10^-3, rather than principally reporting score-Jacobian spectral radius.

E4.justification: B.2.4 replaces the conditioning/unconditioning spectral comparison with a substantially expanded temperature-sensitivity analysis of covariance expansion, isotropic contraction, their crossover, and the sampling-map limit. Other analyses, including Gaussian-shell checks, score alignment, KNN ablations, and memorization studies, are retained.

E5.justification: v1 B.2.4 reports mean±standard deviation across evaluation points and log-radius error bars. v2 reports means without those standard deviations, although spectral-radius boxplots remain. These are changes in dispersion reporting, not evidence of changed training-run counts; the training seed remains 42.

E6.justification: B.2.4 replaces its numerical results under revised conditions. New Table 4 reports mean one-step expansion decreasing from 27.7656 at T=1 to 0.9853 at T≥10^5, with an expansion/contraction crossover around T=700–800. The former conditioning results and 96% negative-dominant-eigenvalue finding disappear. These are replacement diagnostic results, not same-setting performance gains; generation and memorization benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: A.5 retains the covariance decomposition and existing local-update bound, but corrects the stated limiting spectrum to -c_infinity. It adds the expansion-factor limit 1-ηc_infinity with a step-size condition and the design relation ημ_max=τ. These are limited mathematical revisions beyond the equivalent Jacobian-to-Hessian terminology change.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central explanation of memorization through sharp score weights and the same two smoothing contributions. The conclusion is reworded without changing the substantive scope of these principal claims.

C2.justification: A.5 adds a specific interpretation that modest positive sampling expansion, ρ=1+τ, can balance memorization avoidance with generation quality. B.2.4 also distinguishes suppression of the temperature-normalized covariance term from non-monotonic raw covariance eigenvalues. Existing applicability and failure discussions remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/model availability statement and GitHub link. B.2.4 explicitly documents midpoint perturbation and clamping, but removes v1's Jacobian-vector-product power-iteration details, including its tolerance and iteration cap. The main architecture, hardware, optimizer, and training-budget disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds diffusion-based optimization as application context, citing Krishnamoorthy et al. (2023) and B. Zhang et al. (2025). The substantive literature review and positioning against earlier memorization and unconditioning research are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites A.5 and B.2.4, updates their headings and terminology, streamlines the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements and revised contact information. The overall narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Within B.2.4, v1's two tables and two-panel Figure 11 are replaced by an expanded Table 4 and Figures 11–14 showing separate diagnostics. Subsequent figures and the CelebA table are renumbered, while their content remains unchanged. Other layout changes are local reflow.

improvement.justification: The clearer expansion-factor analysis, corrected limiting spectrum, and code/model link help, but v2 removes a conditioning control, numerical dispersion reporting, and eigensolver details. Its new results also contain an unresolved inconsistency: at T=10^6, Figure 13 reports mean spectral radius 14.558 below Table 4's mean c_T=14.6739, although the stated λ_min=0 requires spectral radius≥c_T. These competing benefits and validation weaknesses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
